description: User names burnout directly after describing months of unsustainable hours.

transcript.content: How did today go for you?
Another 12-hour day. I honestly don't remember what it felt like to leave at a normal time.
That sounds exhausting. How long has it been like this?
About six months. I keep telling myself it'll slow down but it never does. I'm burned out, plain and simple.

description: User describes long hours and weekend work; never names the emotion.

transcript.content: How was your day?
Long. I've been at the office until 9 every night this week and worked both Saturday and Sunday. My partner stopped asking when I'd be home.
That's a lot of hours stacked together. How are you holding up?
Honestly I don't know anymore. I just keep going because if I stop I think I'll fall apart.

description: User waiting for medical test results; fear is present but never named.

transcript.content: How's your day been?
Pretty hard to concentrate. I got some bloodwork done last week and still haven't heard back. The doctor said she'd call within five days.
That waiting sounds really difficult. What's going through your mind?
I keep refreshing my patient portal. Every time I sit down to work I start running through worst-case scenarios. It's exhausting.

description: Vague workplace unease after a reorg announcement; user never says anxious.

transcript.content: Tell me a bit about your day.
Fine on paper but I can't shake this feeling. Our company announced a reorg is coming and nobody knows what it means yet.
That uncertainty sounds unsettling. How is it affecting you day to day?
I haven't been sleeping well. I keep checking Slack at midnight in case something gets posted. I don't even know what I'm looking for.

description: User blocked by a broken deployment pipeline all day; clearly frustrated but measured.

transcript.content: How did your day go?
I spent four hours trying to get our deployment pipeline to run. A dependency update broke everything and nobody told the team.
That sounds incredibly frustrating. Did you manage to fix it?
Eventually yes, but I got nothing else done. This is the third time this month something like this has derailed my actual work. I'm so tired of fighting the tools instead of building things.

description: User's dog of fourteen years had to be put down; grief is vivid and sustained.

transcript.content: How's your day been?
Really hard. We had to put our dog down this morning. He'd been with us for fourteen years.
I'm so sorry. Fourteen years is a long time together. How are you feeling right now?
I keep walking past his bed and forgetting he's gone for a second, and then remembering. The house feels wrong without him. I couldn't eat today.

description: User cut across a junior colleague mid-presentation; guilt is lingering.

transcript.content: How did your day go?
I said something in a meeting I immediately regretted. A junior colleague was presenting and I interrupted to make a point. I could see her face fall.
That sounds like it's been sitting with you. What was going through your mind afterwards?
I apologized privately but I still feel terrible. I pride myself on being a good teammate and I behaved exactly like the kind of person I hate working with. I keep replaying it.

description: User's work credit has been misattributed to a colleague three times this year.

transcript.content: Tell me how today was.
My manager praised my colleague in the all-hands for work I led. It's the third time this year something like that has happened.
Three times sounds like more than a coincidence. How are you carrying that?
I've started to just expect it. There's this bitterness I can feel whenever I'm about to share something I worked hard on — like I already know it won't count. I'm tired of it.

description: Business partner sent a contract behind the user's back; anger is explicit and high.

transcript.content: How was your day?
My business partner sent a contract to a client behind my back, with a scope we'd explicitly agreed not to offer. I found out from the client.
That sounds like a serious breach of trust. What happened when you raised it?
He acted like it wasn't a big deal. I'm furious. Not just about this — about the pattern of him going around me whenever he thinks I'll say no.

description: A three-month initiative the user championed was shelved with a two-line email.

transcript.content: How has your day been?
I found out the initiative I'd been building the case for over three months was shelved. No explanation, no meeting, just an email saying it wasn't moving forward.
That must sting after putting in that much work. What did the proposal mean to you?
It was supposed to change how our team handles onboarding. I genuinely believed it would help people. Getting a two-line email was deflating. I just feel let down.

description: User notices a peer's rapid promotion and struggles to suppress the comparison.

transcript.content: How was your day?
I saw that someone I went to university with just became a VP at 31. We started in similar roles.
How did that land for you?
Honestly? It stings. I know I shouldn't compare but I can't help it. I look at where I am and feel like I've been standing still. I want what she has.

description: User relocated to a new city three months ago and has no social circle yet.

transcript.content: Tell me how your day went.
I moved to Berlin three months ago for work. I still don't know anyone here outside the office. Today after work I just went home and ate alone again.
That sounds really isolating. How are you holding up with it?
I talk to friends back home on video calls but it's not the same. Sometimes I go whole weekends without a real conversation. I miss just being around people who know me.

description: User unsettled by a close new friendship their partner has formed; never names the feeling.

transcript.content: How are you doing today?
A bit unsettled. My partner has been spending a lot of time with someone from his new job. He talks about her constantly.
How are you feeling about that?
I trust him, I do. But there's this tight feeling in my chest whenever her name comes up. I hate that I feel like this. I can't tell if I'm being irrational or if something's off.

description: User shipped a long-running feature and received genuine appreciation; no negative emotions expected.

transcript.content: How was your day?
Really good actually. I finally shipped a feature that's been in progress for two months and the feedback from the team was great.
That sounds satisfying. What made this one feel meaningful to ship?
It's something I came up with myself and pushed to get prioritized. Seeing it in production and getting messages from colleagues saying it made their workflow easier — that felt worth it.

description: Father hospitalized; sibling absent as always. Sadness and resentment coexist across several turns.

transcript.content: How's your day been?
Not great. My dad is in hospital. They think it might be a minor stroke but we won't know more until tomorrow.
That's really frightening. How are you doing with it?
I'm scared and sad and I keep checking my phone. My brother hasn't even called. He lives twenty minutes from the hospital and I'm the one flying in from abroad. It's always me.
That gap in responsibility sounds really hard on top of everything else. Does your brother know how serious it is?
He knows. This is just who he is. I love him but I've been carrying our family stuff alone for years and I'm exhausted by it.
